newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes still costly, Latin trade busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes still costly, Latin trade busy.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes still looked prohibitive Thursday despite a moderate widening of the Atlantic arbitrage caused by Dec Brent contract expiry on the London IPE, while reginal Latin trade was buoyant.
The Dec West Texas Intermediate/Brent spread was around 53 cents late in the day, up about 20 cents from Wednesday.
Traders speculated, however, that one million barrels of Brent was sold by a European refiner into eastern Canada this week, after offers were heard around WTI +15 cents cif.
Another European trader also offered a part cargo of Brent at WTI +5 cents cif, for late Nov arrival.
In Latin America, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP bought 250,000 barrels of Argentine Santa Cruz crude and 380,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente at WTI-related prices in its latest purchase tender.
The Oriente purchase surprised some traders because Oriente has an API gravity of 26 degrees, and ANCAP was looking to pick up cargoes of at least API 29 degrees.
Elsewhere, Total sold 550,000 barrels of Cusiana crude for around 40 cents premium to Feb WTI fob for mid-December.
Argentine YPF is selling 380,000 barrels of Escalante for Dec 16-17, asking a price of Jan WTI minus $3 a barrel, trade sources said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, two full cargoes of Jan paper Brent were traded at $23.95 a barrel and a third traded at $23.88 a barrel, up 3-5 cents from the IPE close.
Intermonth spreads were stronger, with Brent Dec/Jan traded at 30 cents, up five cents from the London session.
